Used to + a bare verb is a past habit and never has be: I used to work nights (раньше работал). The classic mistake is I'm used to work here — say I'm used to working here or I used to work here. Both are pronounced with an s sound: YOOST.

entries.meaning: Helpful for doing or getting something. ---
examples: That's a useful tip, thanks.
A second key would be useful for the neighbors.
It's useful to know a little Spanish around here.
entries.takes: for + noun or -ing; to + a person; to-infinitive (useful to know)

entries.meaning: Useless has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A phone with no signal is useless.
It's useless to argue with him.
These old batteries are useless.
I'm useless at remembering names.
He's useless in the kitchen.

senses.head: Not useful; of no help at all
examples: A phone with no signal is useless.
It's useless to argue with him.
These old batteries are useless.

senses.head: Very bad at doing something — informal
examples: I'm useless at remembering names.
He's useless in the kitchen.

entries.takes: at + noun or -ing in the informal 'bad at' sense (useless at math)

entries.meaning: Easy to use or understand, especially for people who are not experts. ---
examples: The new dashboard is much more user-friendly.
We need a user-friendly version of the manual.
Their checkout process isn't very user-friendly.
entries.русский: удобный для пользователя, простой в обращении

entries.meaning: Happening or done most of the time; normal for this person or situation. ---
examples: We met at our usual table.
It's usual to tip about twenty percent.
She took the usual route home.
entries.position: both — mostly before a noun; after a verb usually with it: It's usual to tip
entries.takes: for + noun with a to-infinitive (It's usual for guests to bring something)
entries.contrast: As usual is fixed (He was late, as usual), and the usual is a noun (I'll have the usual). Don't mix the adjective usual with the adverb usually: my usual seat / I usually sit here.

entries.meaning: Charging interest at an unfairly or illegally high rate. ---
examples: The lawsuit calls the fees usurious.
Payday lenders charge usurious rates.
The contract was thrown out as usurious.
entries.contrast: Formal, mostly legal and financial. The noun is usury, YOO-zhuh-ree: lending money at illegally high interest.

entries.meaning: Utilitarian has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The kitchen is plain and utilitarian.
They chose utilitarian furniture that could take a beating.
He made a utilitarian argument for the policy.
The debate turned into a cold utilitarian calculation.

senses.head: Made to be useful rather than attractive
examples: The kitchen is plain and utilitarian.
They chose utilitarian furniture that could take a beating.

senses.head: Relating to utilitarianism, the idea that the right action brings the most good to the most people
examples: He made a utilitarian argument for the policy.
The debate turned into a cold utilitarian calculation.

entries.meaning: Utility has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He's a utility infielder who can catch, too.
Every crew needs one utility player who can cover anything.
We put utility shelving in the garage.
It's a utility knife, not a fancy one.

senses.head: Able to play several positions or do several different jobs
examples: He's a utility infielder who can catch, too.
Every crew needs one utility player who can cover anything.

senses.head: Made for plain practical use rather than for looks
examples: We put utility shelving in the garage.
It's a utility knife, not a fancy one.

entries.contrast: In utility bill, utility company and utility room this is the noun utility used as a modifier. The adjective proper means 'able to fill several roles' (a utility infielder) or 'plain and practical' (utility shelving).

entries.meaning: The greatest possible — used to stress how much. ---
examples: This is a matter of the utmost importance.
Handle the samples with the utmost care.
He has the utmost respect for her.
entries.position: attributive only — of the utmost importance
entries.contrast: Also a noun: She did her utmost. Don't confuse it with uppermost, which is about position. The variant uttermost is literary.

entries.meaning: Imagining or aiming at a perfect society, often unrealistically.
examples: It's a utopian vision with no plan to pay for it.
The commune started out with utopian ideals.
Critics called the proposal utopian.
entries.contrast: Capitalized when it points to Thomas More's Utopia, lowercase in ordinary use. It usually hints that the plan is too perfect to work.
